newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm exports climb to $5.2 bln in Oct - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm exports climb to $5.2 bln in Oct - USDA.

text.p: The Agriculture Department Monday said U.S. agricultural exports climbed to $5.2 billion in October, up 20 percent from September and two percent higher than October 1995.

In a monthly trade report, USDA's Economic Research Service said U.S. corn exports in October were 3.7 million tonnes, up 44 percent from September but down 31 percent from a year ago. Corn shipments to Mexico nearly doubled from September, climbing to 484,000 tonnes, it added.
USDA said U.S. soybean exports more than doubled in October to 2.6 million tonnes and were up 24 percent from a year ago.
October beef exports to Japan increased 17 percent from the previous month to 26,000 tonnes, the highest level since July 1996, the department said in the trade report.
Poultry meat exports continued to be strong, climbing to $254 million, an 18 percent increase over a year ago and 20 percent higher than September.
The department said exports of high value products hit nearly $3 billion in October, up six percent from a year ago.
U.S. agricultural imports were $3 billion, 18 percent above a year ago, USDA said.
